column3: Close to the Hebrew.
“Rushed” is rendered “rushed greedily,” and “young of cattle” as “calves.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “they” as those who told Saul.
NASB renders “and” between ox and sheep as “or,” and “in his hand” as “with him.”
“He began to build an altar” is rendered “it was the first altar that he built.”

“Corners of the people” is rendered “chiefs of the people,” and “know” as “investigate.”
Close to the Hebrew; “though it is in Jonathan” renders “for if it is in Jonathan.”
Close to the Hebrew; “on one side” is rendered “on the other side” for the second group.
NASB follows the short Hebrew text, without the longer Septuagint prayer, reading תָמִים as “a perfect lot.” “Went out” is rendered “escaped.”
“Make fall” is rendered “Cast lots.”
Close to the Hebrew; “here I am, I will die” is rendered “Here I am, I must die!”
NASB supplies “to me” in the oath formula.
“Redeemed” is rendered “rescued.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “pursuing.”
“He acted wickedly” is rendered “he inflicted punishment.”
“Did strength” is rendered “acted valiantly,” and “Amalek” as “the Amalekites.”
